chapter_title: Practical Consequences, Predictive Power, and Use of OC Core 1.3
appendix_title: Practical Utility and Model Comparison Atlas

key_points: The theorem-native domain lanes are usable under explicit theorem, data-route, and falsifier discipline; the cross-domain route-selection lane is operationally supported within bounds and is used for packet selection rather than as a domain-level theorem claim.

Its closed practical value is not unrestricted universal prediction; it is lawful packet selection, bounded residual prediction, anomaly screening, state-transition auditing, regime-shift monitoring, and cross-domain route selection within one source-bound routing framework.
The atlas also keeps 3 frontier-program rows and 1 hypothesis-only row explicit so practical ambition does not masquerade as finished closure.

use_case_rows.problem_class: Strict closure certification and counterexample elimination
use_case_rows.what_can_be_predicted_or_done: Certify whether a bounded formal object or question packet survives strict closure and counterexample search under the locked mathematical lane.
use_case_rows.how_to_apply: Encode the object in the admissible exact-question format, run the strict terminalization and counterexample route, and accept only a replayable proof or an explicit counterexample.
use_case_rows.scope_boundary: Applies only to the bounded exact question families already represented in the mathematical anchor. It does not claim a general uniqueness theorem beyond the current impossibility boundary.
use_case_rows.output_or_decision: A replayable accept or reject result together with minimal denominator, augmentation rank, or surviving counterexample classification.
serious_model_families: Classical exact proof and exhaustive-search families
use_case_rows.what_remains_open: Global uniqueness beyond the current impossibility boundary remains frontier territory rather than a promoted practical result.

use_case_rows.what_can_be_predicted_or_done: Audit bounded constants, Balmer-line families, and transport-scaling envelopes on held-out benchmark families and flag out-of-envelope residual behavior.
use_case_rows.how_to_apply: Bind the target observable family to the locked K1/K2/K9/K10 packet, pull the pinned official dataset route, and run the declared held-out replay under the locked sigma policy.
use_case_rows.scope_boundary: Applies only to the promoted constants, Balmer spectra, and transport-scaling packet. It does not replace unrestricted microphysical law solving or the full local-derivation stack.
required_inputs_or_observables: official constants or spectra or transport benchmark family
use_case_rows.output_or_decision: A pass or fail residual verdict, anomaly prioritization, and a decision about whether the family remains inside the promoted packet.
benchmark_comparators: bounded residual fit without theorem trace
serious_model_families: Precision quantum electrodynamics and atomic-structure theory
use_case_rows.what_remains_open: Full unrestricted microphysical derivation outside the promoted residual packet remains open and may not be advertised as closed by this use-case row.

use_case_rows.what_can_be_predicted_or_done: Launch a lawful frontier program for broader field, particle, or transport families while keeping theorem, parameter-law, held-out, and comparator gates explicit.
use_case_rows.how_to_apply: Start from the closed residual packet, declare the new observable family ex ante, and reopen theorem, parameter-law, replay, and comparator gates before any outward claim.
use_case_rows.scope_boundary: No broader microphysical lane is currently promoted by this row. It is a disciplined research program, not a deployable closed packet.

operational_playbooks.title: Strict closure and counterexample playbook
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to determine whether a bounded exact question already lies inside the promoted mathematical anchor or should be rejected by the strict counterexample route.
procedure_steps: Encode the target object in the admissible exact-question form.
Run the declared terminalization and counterexample search.
Accept the result only if the replay is deterministic and survivor-free.
Escalate to frontier if the question leaves the declared exact scope.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A replayable proof result, a surviving counterexample, or a lawful frontier demotion.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: The playbook is limited to the exact mathematical anchor and does not advertise broader uniqueness claims than the current proof machinery supports.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop if the object cannot be encoded in the admissible exact-question format or if a surviving counterexample remains after the declared search.

operational_playbooks.title: Bounded constants, spectra, and transport audit
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to decide whether a constants family, spectral family, or transport family belongs inside the promoted physics packet or should be escalated as an anomaly.
procedure_steps: Map the observable family to the promoted physics packet.
Load the pinned official dataset and the locked held-out split.
Run the declared residual replay and inspect sign or order constraints.
Accept the family only if the replay stays inside the promoted tolerance band.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A bounded inclusion, anomaly, or escalation verdict for the target physical family.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: The playbook stays inside the promoted residual packet and does not authorize unrestricted physical universalization.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop and demote to frontier if the observable family requires a widened scope, hidden fit freedom, or a post-hoc split change.

operational_playbooks.title: Thermochemical, spectral, and kinetic packet audit
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to decide whether a bounded compound family or reaction class lies inside the promoted chemistry packet or should be escalated as an out-of-envelope case.
procedure_steps: Map the chemistry lane to the promoted packet and observable family.
Load the pinned reference tables and the locked held-out split.
Run the declared replay on thermochemical, spectral, or kinetic outputs.
Accept the lane only if the held-out family remains inside the promoted tolerance band.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A bounded inclusion, anomaly, or escalation verdict for the target chemistry lane.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: The playbook is limited to the promoted chemistry packet and does not authorize unrestricted universal chemistry claims.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop and demote to frontier if the lane requires hidden fit freedom, widened scope, or post-hoc split changes.

operational_playbooks.title: Bounded biological signature and onset screening
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to decide whether a bounded assay lane belongs inside the promoted biological packet or should be escalated as an unresolved biological signature family.
required_inputs_or_observables: declared signature, transition, or onset observable
procedure_steps: Map the biological lane to the promoted packet and observable family.
Load the locked multi-dataset route and held-out split.
Run the declared replay on expression, transition-order, or onset outputs.
Accept the lane only if the held-out datasets stay inside the promoted signature envelope.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A bounded inclusion, anomaly, or escalation verdict for the target biological lane.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: The playbook stays inside the promoted biological packet and does not authorize unrestricted biological universalization.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop and demote to frontier if the lane depends on a single dataset family, hidden fit freedom, or a widened biological claim boundary.

operational_playbooks.title: Bounded macro-trajectory and regime-shift monitoring
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when the task is to decide whether an official macro-process series remains inside the promoted systems packet or should be escalated as a turning-point or regime anomaly.
procedure_steps: Map the macro-process lane to the promoted systems packet.
Load the pinned official series and the locked held-out interval.
Run the declared residual and turning-point replay.
Accept the lane only if held-out intervals remain inside the promoted trajectory and regime envelope.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A bounded inclusion, anomaly, or escalation verdict for the target systems lane.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: The playbook stays inside the promoted systems packet and does not authorize unrestricted civilizational prediction.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop and demote to frontier if the lane requires out-of-band trajectory behavior, a widened horizon, or post-hoc interval selection.

operational_playbooks.title: Cross-domain packet selection and escalation playbook
operational_playbooks.when_to_use: Use when a scientific or engineering problem touches more than one domain lane and the team must decide which closed packet, comparator family, and evidence route should govern the next action.
procedure_steps: Map the target problem to the narrowest lawful observable family.
Select the closed packet whose theorem-to-observable map already governs that family.
Check same-claim baselines and serious comparators before claiming advantage.
Escalate only when the closed packet boundary is reached and the atlas permits the translation.
operational_playbooks.output_or_decision: A lawful route-selection decision with explicit packet, comparator, falsifier, and escalation boundaries.
operational_playbooks.scope_boundary: This playbook coordinates closed packets; it does not license unconstrained whole-world prediction.
operational_playbooks.failure_boundary: Stop and demote to frontier if the observable family is outside every closed packet or if two candidate routes produce incompatible bounded verdicts.
